shared_qualifications: C1: Source uses saturated Ag/AgCl; the tip is approximately 5 mm above the specimen in the 80 +/- 2 C tests (PDF pp.2-3). Reference-electrode thermal calibration is not specified. The affine formula is E_SCE=E_AgCl+E_AgCl_vs_SHE-E_SCE_vs_SHE. HORIBA lists +0.199 and +0.244 V at 25 C for the respective standard-KCl electrodes (https://www.horiba.com/twn/water-quality/support/electrochemistry/the-basis-of-ph/electrical-potential-of-reference-electrode/), which would yield a -45 mV offset under that explicitly hypothetical 25 C convention. It numerically reproduces the CRA cells but is not established for the hot reference conditions. Therefore potential agreement remains not_comparable; no 25 C offset is claimed as a calibrated 80 C conversion.
Table 2 distinguishes Ep (slow stepped polarization), Ep/s (scratching), and Epp (protection). Neither scratching thresholds nor first-pit transients are substituted for the six scan Ep records.
The source changes potential by 10 mV each hour; 10/3600=0.0027778 mV/s is only an equivalent nominal average ramp. It remains a staircase experiment, not a continuous sweep.
